label: Component percentage bait, source activation and truthful negative evidence
evidence_type: synthetic engineering fixtures; no real paper performance claim
task: Reduce p99 request TTFT for current H200 DP4/EP4 deployment. Produce the next most useful hypothesis and evaluation design using these records. GPU execution and service changes are forbidden now; ordinary source inspection and CPU arithmetic are allowed. Do not invent a missing timing.

evidence.text: Fixture PR FAST-C replaces a CPU completion callback with a batch callback. Author reports callback duration 100us to 40us at batch size 64 on a CPU microbenchmark; the callback runs once after request completion. A social summary calls this 60% faster inference.

The pinned deployed source already includes FAST-C, but resolved config has batching disabled. Enabling it is a possible configuration intervention. Current agent-75 emits 1024 output tokens per request; request arrival and completion timestamps exist, callback timings and CPU utilization do not.
A separate GPU all-to-all patch FAST-G reports 18% throughput gain on eight SM100 GPUs, but its new launch path requires SM100 instructions and has no SM90 fallback. It is not installed.

A prior attempt enabling callback batching failed at startup because an optional CPU package was missing. It produced no traffic and no serving measurements. The package is now available in a staging environment, not yet the serving image.

request: State which ideas remain feasible, what the prior failure means, what service benefit can and cannot be inferred, and the cheapest next investigation. Include counterevidence and stop/inconclusive criteria.
